objective.statement: Restore a portable global cargo-pgrx fallback for JCode and operator shells by delegating to the Engine-owned Nix cargo-pgrx 0.18.0 package instead of the host-incompatible AVX-512 Cargo install.
objective.measure: Home Manager owns an executable ~/.local/bin/cargo-pgrx entrypoint; cargo pgrx --help exits 0 from a normal shell and an Engine workspace; the Engine fabric shell remains recursion-free; no new stored SIGILL coredump appears.

need.statement: JCode and operator shells need a portable cargo-pgrx 0.18.0 fallback on this Zen 3 host.
need.baseline: The global ~/.cargo/bin/cargo-pgrx 0.18.0 exits 132 on an AVX-512 vmovdqu64 instruction and has seven JCode-worker coredump records. The Engine fabrics/data Nix package of the same version exits 0.
need.consequence_of_no_action: VectorDrive and other Engine pgrx work can crash before tests run whenever a worker resolves the global Cargo install outside the nested fabric shell.
assumptions: Engine fabrics/data remains the package authority for cargo-pgrx 0.18.0.
alternatives_considered: Rebuild another unmanaged global Cargo install
Copy the current Nix store binary into ~/.cargo/bin
Change Engine source or every worker command

purpose: Restore a portable global cargo-pgrx fallback for JCode and operator shells by delegating to the Engine-owned Nix cargo-pgrx 0.18.0 package instead of the host-incompatible AVX-512 Cargo install.
consumer: JCode swarm workers and the mhugo operator on cc-se-sto-devbox-01.
contract: Home Manager owns an executable ~/.local/bin/cargo-pgrx entrypoint that resolves a current Engine workspace fabrics/data flake when available, otherwise the canonical Engine fabric, delegates all arguments to that flake's cargo-pgrx 0.18.0 without recursion, makes cargo pgrx --help exit 0, and leaves JCode services and Engine source unchanged.
failure_boundary: The repair is confined to a managed dotfiles wrapper and removal of the incompatible unmanaged Cargo install after activation proof. Do not change Engine source, JCode service wiring, other Cargo tools, or active workspaces.

evidence.description: A contract test proves Home Manager ownership, nearest-workspace resolution, canonical fallback, argument forwarding, and recursion avoidance.
After activation, cargo pgrx --help exits 0 from /home/mhugo and an Engine workspace, reports version 0.18.0, and creates no new stored SIGILL coredump.

falsifier.claim: The managed wrapper restores a portable cargo-pgrx 0.18.0 fallback.

executable_check.description: Run the wrapper contract and live help probes; any non-zero exit, wrong flake selection, recursion, version drift, or new stored SIGILL coredump falsifies the claim.

non_goals: Repackage cargo-pgrx outside the Engine fabric
Change Engine source or pgrx test configuration
Change JCode model routing or worker capacity
Clean unrelated Cargo packages, caches, worktrees, or builds
invariants: Engine fabrics/data remains the cargo-pgrx package authority
The nested Engine fabric shell resolves its Nix package before ~/.local/bin and cannot recurse
JCode services, sockets, sessions, and active workspaces remain intact
No secret material enters source or evidence
All VCS actions use the repository-owned repo vcs facade

assumptions.statement: The Engine fabrics/data flake continues to expose cargo-pgrx 0.18.0 in its development shell.
assumptions.falsifier: nix develop path:/home/mhugo/code/singularity-engine/fabrics/data --command cargo-pgrx pgrx --help exits non-zero or reports another version.

assumptions.statement: ~/.local/bin precedes the unmanaged Cargo bin directory in managed interactive and non-interactive shells.
assumptions.falsifier: A fresh managed shell resolves cargo-pgrx to ~/.cargo/bin before ~/.local/bin.

plane_constraints: Home Manager owns the global entrypoint; Engine fabrics/data owns the cargo-pgrx package; JCode only consumes the command.
